structured.approach: I followed the data-science-steps procedure for DS-05 and implemented exactly the components DS-04 listed in task.components (CMP-1 to CMP-3), using the signatures and rules in feat.design B2.2 and the acceptance criteria in feat.stories. This step may write only src/ap_forecast/, docs/ and README.md, so I left the planned tests (CMP-4, CMP-5) to DS-06. I added risk.py, made the additive risk=None change to explain.py, and in __init__.py exported vendor_risk and stepped the minor version. I documented the change in README.md and a new docs/ap_forecast.md, then ran /usr/bin/python3 ci.py once and checked the changed files with git status and git diff --stat. This step's hook allows only ci.py and read-only git, so I could not run the new paths in an ad-hoc script. I did not pad coverage by other means. I reported the coverage shortfall honestly and wrote task.code.md.
tools_used: Bash (/usr/bin/python3 ci.py, git status, git diff --stat)

claims.text: New module src/ap_forecast/risk.py defines HIGH_ABOVE_DAYS = 30, MEDIUM_ABOVE_DAYS = 10 and vendor_risk(history), which calls predict_delay_days once and compares with strict '>' (high above 30, medium above 10, else low); it imports only predict_delay_days, not explain.

build_explanation_request gains risk=None as its last parameter and appends ' Risk level: {risk}.' to the prompt only when risk is not None; provider, model and max_tokens still come from config or load_config().
__init__.py exports vendor_risk in __all__ and steps the version from 0.9.0 to 0.10.0 (a minor step, as DD-11 asks).

CI after the changes: compile true, 3 tests run with 0 failures and 0 errors, no static issues, coverage 83.3% against the 90% gate, so overall passed is false. Missed lines are risk.py 17-20 and explain.py 21.

The tests that cover the missed lines (CMP-4 tests/test_risk.py and CMP-5 additions to tests/test_forecast.py) are planned in task.components, but tests/ is outside this step's write scope (src/ap_forecast/, docs/, README.md).
The change adds no secret, network call or database change; models.json holds only provider, model and max_tokens.
Boundary behaviour required by L-007 is implemented: a prediction of exactly 30 gives 'medium' and exactly 10 gives 'low'.
Changed paths are README.md, src/ap_forecast/__init__.py and src/ap_forecast/explain.py (3 tracked files, 34 insertions, 5 deletions), plus the new docs/ and src/ap_forecast/risk.py.
The repository rule is to keep existing public signatures and add new functions for new behaviour; the only signature change is a trailing default parameter.

open_questions: CQ-C1: CI fails only the 90% coverage gate (83.3%) after DS-05, because the new tests belong under tests/, which this step may not write. Should DS-05 accept a coverage-only failure that DS-06 closes with the planned CMP-4 and CMP-5 tests, or should DS-05's write scope include tests/?
CQ-C2: Confirm 0.10.0 as the package version (CQ-DS-2 from task.components).
Carried: CQ-DS-1 (test file split), CQ-DS-3 (per-environment secrets record), RAQ-1 (branching), TQ-8 and PQ-5 (STORY-04 release), PQ-1, TQ-5, TQ-4.
structured.summary: The DS-05 code is in place on feature/story in ap_forecast, but CI does not pass yet: coverage is 83.3% against the 90% gate. Everything else in CI passes: it compiles, the 3 existing tests pass, and the static checks find no issues. The 5 uncovered lines are the new vendor_risk body and the risk append in build_explanation_request. Their planned tests go under tests/, which this step may not change, so DS-06 adds them (CQ-C1). The change adds risk.py with vendor_risk and its two threshold constants, gives build_explanation_request an optional last parameter risk=None, exports vendor_risk and moves the version from 0.9.0 to 0.10.0. README.md and a new docs/ap_forecast.md document the functions. The new behaviour was not run in this step, because only the CI command and read-only git are allowed here. Nothing is committed; task.code.md records the details.
